alex: Ran a 30m flamegraph across the host path for the streaming API. Seeing a weird bump after switching to http2 writev aggregation. CPU on host threads up ~18% for p99 decode paths. Need quick triage.

tara: thanks for the heads-up. can you paste the flame snippet and the exact commit?

alex: commit c3f9b2d (http2: batch writev + hpack reuse). small PR but changed the write path. snippet below:

alex: ```
PROFILE_SUMMARY
tokenize_input        120.3ms (16%)
parse_request         85.8ms  (11%)
grpc_writev           140.9ms (19%)  <-- spike after change
http2_frame           98.7ms  (13%)
serialize_chunks      62.1ms  (8%)
kv_cache_lookup       41.2ms  (5%)
other_syscalls        232.0ms (28%)
end-to-end p99 host-overhead +18%
```

ben: grpc_writev jump is interesting. are we coalescing too aggressively and causing extra copy for small chunks?

sofia: also check tokenization: I see tokenization time moved up for multi-part streams. maybe framing changes are invalidating prefix cache keys so kv_cache_lookup drops hit-rate and tokenization reruns.

alex: good call. hit-rate went 87% -> 64% for prefix keys on this canary cohort. I have a scatter of request lengths and chunk boundaries that show more boundary-shift when we coalesce frames.

tara: possible fixes: 1) limit coalescing for HTTP2 streams when request indicates streaming tokens (preserve chunk boundaries), 2) normalize framing before cache key, 3) compute cache key from logical tokens instead of raw bytes (if cheap).

ben: for kernel selection / batching heuristics side: we could change the runtime hint to prefer smaller kernels when host CPU overhead is high, that reduces decode pressure and may offset host CPU. but this only helps tail for large seq.

sofia: I can run a microbench: disable http2 batch writev on the canary and re-run the p99. also test a quick pre-tokenize at edge to avoid host tokenization spike.

alex: perf numbers from quick rollback: disabling http2 writev aggregation drops grpc_writev from 140.9ms -> 88.2ms, host p99 -10% vs canary baseline. kv_cache hit-rate back to 85%. so appears coalescing mutated frame boundaries used by the parse-to-cache-layer.

tara: ok we have two angles: short-term rollback + add a regression test for cache-key entanglement with framing. long-term: change coalescer to annotate logical boundaries or compute cache keys after normalization.

ben: also propose a lightweight batching heuristic: if host cpu percentile > threshold, prefer immediate send for small frames (avoid extra copies). simple and reversible by config.

sofia: I'll open a follow-up PR to: revert coalescing in the canary, add a unit for cache-key normalization, and add a microbenchmark that simulates streaming chunk patterns.

alex: created ticket INF-9142 with logs and flamegraph link: https://redwood-internal/issue/INF-9142. attaching quick trace: /traces/2833141592

runtime-bot: deploy v2.11.3-canary to cluster "ingress-canary-a" triggered by @alex at 2026-03-18T10:10:00Z :rocket:

tara: update cadence: revert in canary now, run 2x 1h benchmarks (mixed lengths ~12k reqs), if stable roll to 10% for 3h then full. sofia can you own the benchmarks and ben the config toggle?

sofia: on it. will report numbers in thread.

ben: I'll draft a runtime flag `http2.coalesce_mode=adaptive_or_off` and default to adaptive but allow off for canary.

alex: thanks team. next actions summarized:
- sofia: rollback coalescing in canary + run benchmarks (ETA 2h)
- ben: flag + heuristic for host-cpu threshold (ETA EOD)
- tara: add regression test and follow-up design doc for cache-key normalization (ETA 2d)
- alex: monitor canary and update INF-9142

alex: :thumbsup:
